private_note: I get a one-in-five draw, so I weigh both the average and the floor. Alder has the same average as Today (100) but lifts the bottom from 22 to 32 and adds guaranteed health coverage, at a small cost at the top: near-free insurance. Cedar's higher average comes with a brutal 15 floor and no coverage. Hazel and Birch give up 20-plus of average to buy a floor; too expensive. Alder is also the most plausible route to 9 votes.
statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows which fifth we will land in, so each of us should ask which plan is the best bet for our own household. Alder keeps the average household income exactly where it is today, 100, while raising the bottom from 22 to 32 and guaranteeing everyone health coverage. Even drawing the top fifth, you give up only about 4 percent. That is cheap insurance against a one-in-five chance of hardship. Cedar offers a higher average, but a one-in-five chance of living on 15 with no coverage is a serious gamble for a generation. Birch and Hazel buy a higher floor by cutting the average by a fifth: we would all likely be poorer. We need nine votes or we are stuck with today's arrangements, which Alder simply improves on. I urge you to rally around Alder now.
